prompt_text: My roof has hail damage in Denver. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live web access to look up current contractors for you, so I can’t give a verified, up‑to‑the‑minute list of specific Denver roofers. I can, however, help you in two ways right away:

- If you tell me your neighborhood or ZIP code I’ll tell you exactly what to search for and what to look for in the top results so you can quickly identify 3–5 good local companies to call.
- Or I can give an immediate checklist, script and comparison sheet you can use when you call contractors and your insurer — plus red flags to avoid — so you choose the best roofer and avoid storm‑chasing scams.

Below is the practical, ready‑to‑use guidance I recommend for hail damage in Denver.

Immediate steps (what to do now)
1. Document the damage: take time‑stamped photos and video of your roof, gutters, siding, vehicles and anything else hit by hail.
2. Protect against leaks: if you have active leaks, hire someone for a temporary tarp/patch until the permanent repair is done. Get a written receipt.
3. Call your homeowner’s insurance to report the claim. Ask your adjuster what documentation they need and whether they’ll meet the contractor on site.
4. Get at least 3 written estimates from different roofing contractors (more after large storms is fine). Don’t accept door‑to‑door storm‑chaser offers without checking them thoroughly.

How to find the best companies (quick search tips)
- Search Google with: “roofing contractor Denver [your ZIP] hail damage,” then sort by Google Reviews and look for 4.2+ average with many recent reviews.
- Check Yelp, Angi (Angie’s List), Nextdoor and the BBB for reviews and complaints.
- Look for manufacturers’ certifications on roofer sites (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) — these show training and warranty access.
- Prefer contractors who list a physical Denver‑area office and a local phone number (not just a mobile number or P.O. box).

Must‑ask questions when you call (use this script)
- “How long have you been doing residential roofing in Denver?”
- “Do you have experience handling hail‑damage insurance claims?” (If yes, ask if they’ll work with your adjuster and whether they accompany the adjuster on inspections.)
- “Are you licensed, bonded and insured? Can you send proof of general liability and workers’ comp?”
- “Do you have manufacturer certifications (GAF/OC/CertainTeed)? Which product lines do you install?”
- “What warranties do you provide (manufacturer warranty + workmanship)? How long?”
- “What is your typical schedule after I sign a contract? Do you pull permits for Denver?”
- “Do you require a deposit, and what is the payment schedule?” (Red flag: full payment up front.)
- “Will you provide a written scope of work and an itemized estimate, including material types, disposal, permit costs and cleanup?”

What to compare on estimates (side‑by‑side)
- Scope of work (roof deck repair? flashing? ventilation?)
- Materials (brand, class of shingle, color, underlayment)
- Warranties (manufacturer vs. workmanship; length and transferability)
- Permits and inspections (who pays and pulls the permit?)
- Price, payment schedule and any financing options
- Cleanup and dumpster removal
- Timeline to start and finish

Red flags and things to avoid
- Storm‑chasing crews that appear immediately after a storm claiming “we were in the neighborhood.”
- No verifiable local address or poor online reviews about workmanship or payment disputes.
- Demands for the full contract amount before work begins.
- Pressure to sign a contract that assigns your insurance check to the contractor without you understanding the paperwork.
- Contractors who won’t provide proof of insurance or refuse to sign lien waivers.

Who to prioritize calling
- A reputable local Denver roofing company with long history and good local reviews.
- A roofer who specializes in insurance claims and has experience with Denver hail claims.
- A smaller local roofing company (sometimes more flexible and attentive) for comparison.

If you want, give me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you’d prefer a large company or a local small business. I’ll then:
- Tell you exact search phrases and filters to use,
- Provide a sample short list of candidate company names to look up (based on typical Denver reputations), and
- Produce a one‑page comparison worksheet you can print or use when you call.

Which would you prefer?
